headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold their first three-way meeting

chunks.text: On November 19, 2026, the presidents of the U.S., China and Russia held their [[first-ever]] [[three-way meeting]]. Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin {{sat down}} together in southern China. All three were there for a [[summit]], a meeting of world leaders. It was the yearly summit of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation. This group of 21 Pacific countries and places works together on [[trade]].

verbs.why: The guests sit down at the table before dinner. The students sit down when the teacher walks in. Trump, Xi and Putin sat down together in southern China.

chunks.text: First, Trump met Xi and Putin [[one at a time]]. He called each one his "friend." The three-way talks {{kicked off}} at a [[round table]], with short speeches in front of reporters. "The world is at peace when great powers live in [[harmony]]," Xi said. [[Great powers]] are very strong countries. Trump {{pointed out}} that the three countries have the most [[nuclear weapons]] in the world. He had also said he would {{bring up}} the war in Ukraine. Then the leaders talked [[in private]].

verbs.correct: To begin an event or activity
verbs.wrong: To force someone to leave a place
verbs.why: The festival kicks off with a big parade. Our meetings always kick off at nine. The three-way talks kicked off with short speeches in front of reporters.

verbs.correct: To mention a fact so people notice it
verbs.wrong: To choose someone for a team
verbs.why: My teacher points out my spelling mistakes. The guide points out the oldest building in town. Trump pointed out that the three countries have the most nuclear weapons in the world.

verbs.correct: To start talking about a subject
verbs.why: My dad brings up politics at every family dinner. She never brings up her old job. Trump had said he would bring up the war in Ukraine.

chunks.text: Afterward, the countries released a [[joint statement]], a message from all three. It {{laid out}} four main points. In one, they promised to {{talk over}} ways to reduce the dangers of nuclear weapons. In another, they agreed to {{step up}} the production and [[supply]] of fuels made from oil, such as gasoline. A third point called for changes at the United Nations. The statement {{left out}} the war in Ukraine.

verbs.correct: To explain a plan or idea clearly
verbs.wrong: To put a plan away for later
verbs.why: The coach lays out the plan before each game. A good teacher lays out the rules on the first day. The joint statement laid out four main points.

verbs.correct: To discuss something with other people
verbs.wrong: To sign a deal without reading it
verbs.why: My wife and I talk over big decisions together. Before a trip, we talk over the costs. The three countries promised to talk over ways to reduce the dangers of nuclear weapons.

verbs.correct: To increase the amount of something
verbs.wrong: To leave an important job or post
verbs.why: Factories step up work before Christmas. The city steps up bus service during big games. The three countries agreed to step up the production and supply of fuels made from oil.
He always leaves out the boring parts of the story. Some recipes leave out salt for health reasons. The joint statement left out the war in Ukraine.

chunks.text: On November 20, Trump {{talked up}} the trip at a White House [[news conference]]. He said he and Xi agreed to make [[guardrails]], or safety rules, for [[artificial intelligence]]. He did not {{spell out}} the details. After the trip, he rated it a 12 on a scale of zero to 10. But National Public Radio reported that few real results {{came out of}} the meeting. Putin called the talks very honest and open. He said the leaders {{came away}} understanding one another better.

verbs.correct: To praise something to make it seem better
verbs.wrong: To repeat something so people remember it
verbs.why: Store workers talk up the new phones to every customer. Coaches often talk up young players. On November 20, Trump talked up the trip at a White House news conference.

verbs.correct: To explain every detail of something
verbs.wrong: To take a photo of something
verbs.why: The contract spells out how much you pay each month. My boss spells out what she wants from each of us. Trump did not spell out the details of the AI guardrails.

verbs.correct: To be the result of something
verbs.wrong: To be the cost of something
verbs.why: Good ideas often come out of long talks. Many new friendships come out of sports teams. National Public Radio reported that few real results came out of the meeting.

verbs.correct: To leave a place with a certain feeling
verbs.wrong: To miss a meeting for a certain reason
verbs.why: Most visitors come away happy from the museum. Students often come away from her class with new ideas. Putin said the leaders came away understanding one another better.

mainIdea.s: The leaders of the U.S., China and Russia met together for the first time and released a joint statement. They promised more talks on nuclear dangers, but few real deals came out of it.
mainIdea.why: The three countries agreed to talk over ways to reduce nuclear dangers. National Public Radio reported that few real results came out of the meeting.

mainIdea.s: The leaders of the U.S., China and Russia held a first meeting in southern China. They signed a deal to end the war in Ukraine and agreed to cut the number of their nuclear weapons.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the statement left out the war in Ukraine. The countries only promised to talk over ways to reduce nuclear dangers.

mainIdea.s: Leaders from 21 Pacific countries agreed to lower taxes on goods they sell each other. The group says the new trade plan will start next spring and could make many products cheaper.
mainIdea.why: This story is about the first meeting of Trump, Xi and Putin. They laid out four main points, but none was about lowering taxes on goods.

tf.s: Trump, Xi and Putin sat down together for their first three-way meeting.
tf.why: The three leaders sat down at a round table in southern China on November 19, 2026.

tf.s: The joint statement left out the war in Ukraine.
tf.why: The statement laid out four main points, but none of them was about the war in Ukraine.

tf.s: The three countries agreed to step up the production of fuels made from oil.
tf.why: They promised to step up both the production and the supply of these fuels.

tf.s: The leaders refused to talk over ways to reduce the dangers of nuclear weapons.
tf.why: They promised to talk over ways to reduce these dangers. This was one of the four points in their statement.

tf.s: Trump told reporters that the trip to China was a failure.
tf.why: Trump talked up the trip at a news conference. He rated it a 12 on a scale of zero to 10.

tf.s: Trump gave full details of the AI safety rules he planned with Xi.
tf.why: Trump said he and Xi agreed to make AI guardrails, but he did not spell out the details.

lines.text: Did you see the photos of Trump, Xi and Putin together in China?
I did. All three in one room. [[What a sight]]. That's never happened before.
They {{sat down}} together at a round table.
Was it just a [[photo op]], or did they actually agree on anything?
They released a joint statement. It {{laid out}} four main points.
They promised to {{talk over}} ways to make nuclear weapons less dangerous. And they want to {{step up}} the supply of fuels made from oil.
What about the war in Ukraine?
Trump had said he would {{bring up}} the war, but the statement {{left out}} Ukraine.
So did anything real {{come out of}} it?
Not much, according to NPR. But Trump {{talked up}} the trip anyway. He gave it a 12 out of 10.
Wow. Did he say anything new?
He said he and Xi will make safety rules for AI together. But he didn't {{spell out}} the details.
So nobody knows yet what those rules will be.
Not yet. Still, nuclear safety was [[front and center]].
We'll see if more talks [[move the needle]].

expressions.def: Used to say that something is surprising or special to see

expressions.def: An event planned mostly so people can take nice pictures

expressions.def: In the most important position, where everyone notices it
ex: Safety is front and center in the new plan.

expressions.def: To make a real and noticeable difference
ex: One small ad won't move the needle on sales.
The new law could really move the needle on pollution.
